problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,{u}^{3}-uv⟩$ at the point where $u=2$ and $v=6.$

feedback.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u⟩$ at the point where $u=2$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u)⟩ \\  & =⟨-u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=2$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(2,\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(2,\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(2,\frac{\pi }{2})\times {r}_{v}^{′}(2,\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=2$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}$ correspond to the point 

$$
(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2)=(0,2,2),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨0,\,-2,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨x,\,y-2,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ 0\cdot x+(-2)\cdot (y-2)+2\cdot (z-2) & =0 \\ -2y+2z & =0 \\ y-z & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
